craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of fitted joinery — utsāha as qualifier meets qualified without loss. Two facings, one relation: own-kind vs master-kind tie — nominal mirror kept. Rejected: (a) verbs for nominals → killed by SA mirror. (b) tie→bond → killed: L3 frozen. Read aloud: GRASP-of-KING STANDS-one, FAC-ing ITS-own-KIND — … SHAR-ing THE-mas-ter-KIND's-TIE.

lines: Grasp 'of king' stands one, facing its own kind —
'man' the other, sharing the master-kind's tie.
l4.sanskrit_cite: vimarśo rājña ityekaḥ svasāmānyonmukhaḥ paraḥ svāmisāmānyasaṃbandhasahaḥ puruṣa ityayam

reads_against.argmap: How do the two reflections divide? → 'King' faces own-generality; 'man' faces the master's — two reflections, one relation.
c1_essence: Unity without strain for the consciousness-bodied; the worldly one's reflection-object fixed as difference-pithed non-difference-shining (vv10-11).
Mechanics: one thought un-touched, one word uniting many, helping relation admitted, twoness in manyness, two facings, three thinkings, genitive settling unself-lost (vv12-18).
